items.title: Bob Wilber Interview, 1961-05-01
items.q: I studied under Rufus Airy up at Eastman.

ctx.x: Yeah. Some others. Is it cross finger? No, no. I can't think of the name. But they call it forked fingerings down here. Yeah, yeah. You know, when they leave one finger... Did he ever discuss anything of those kind of...

No, he didn't because of the fact that he played Albert and I played Bane. Oh, that's right. And I had a fairly good basic knowledge of the fingering of the instrument from legitimate study by then, you know. I studied under Rufus Airy up at Eastman. Oh, that's right. Legitimate. And I studied with a man named Dom who played with the Goldman Band in New York. And I'd gone through the Bane, the Lazarus books and the Closet and all those studies.
Speaking of Sidney's lessons again, did he ever advise you how long to practice or...
